2027-07-23.title: Ezekiel the Prophet · Friday of the ninth week after Pentecost
readings: He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son
“The one who endures to the end will be saved”: the beginning of the birth pangs and the good news to all nations
2027-07-23.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam keeps today the memory of Ezekiel the Prophet (എസക്കിയേൽ നിബിയാ, the Panchangam's spelling), the last by date of the Old Testament saints whom it remembers this month, after Aaron, Elijah and Daniel. The Panchangam gives the readings of the weekday only.
2027-07-23.verse: But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
theo: Jesus is sitting on the Mount of Olives when the disciples come to him privately, saying: “Tell us, when will this be, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?” He does not give them a timetable. He gives them a way to live: “Beware that no one leads you astray. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Messiah!’ and they will lead many astray. And you will hear of wars and rumors of wars; see that you are not alarmed; for this must take place, but the end is not yet.” Wars, famines and earthquakes are “but the beginning of the birth pangs”, which means that they are pains that lead to birth, not to death. Then comes the harder word about the disciples themselves: they will be hated, many will fall away, false prophets will arise, and “because of the increase of lawlessness, the love of many will grow cold.” In the floods that have come upon Kerala in recent years, we have seen both: fear, and also the warm love of neighbour for neighbour, the fishermen with their boats and the people who opened their churches and homes. Jesus says: “But the one who endures to the end will be saved. And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the world, as a testimony to all the nations; and then the end will come.” The Church has never turned these words into a calendar. She hears in them a call to watchfulness, to endurance, and to mission.

Today the Panchangam remembers Ezekiel, a prophet for hard times. He was a priest, “Ezekiel son of Buzi,” who was carried into exile with the leaders of Judah, and in the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin, as he was “among the exiles by the river Chebar,” he writes, “the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.” He saw the glory of the Lord, not in the Temple in Jerusalem, but beside a canal in Babylon: the Lord had not been left behind in the ruined city, and he came to his people in exile. Ezekiel was told to eat a scroll, and he says: “Then I ate it; and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.” The word of God is sweet even when it announces hard things. And he was made a sentinel: “Mortal, I have made you a sentinel for the house of Israel; whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you shall give them warning from me.” The watchman on the wall is the picture of today's Gospel: beware, do not be led astray, stay awake. A watchman does not frighten people for the sake of it. He cries out so that they may live.

But Ezekiel is also the prophet of the new heart. To the exiles who thought that all was over, the Lord promised: “A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.” In the vision of the dry bones, the Lord asks: “Mortal, can these bones live?” and he commands the prophet to speak: “I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.” The Church has long heard in this vision the promise of resurrection and of the gift of the Holy Spirit, which we remember in this season after Pentecost. At the end of the book, Ezekiel sees water flowing from below the threshold of the temple toward the east, growing into a river, so that “everything will live where the river goes.” In July in Kerala, when our rivers are full and the land is green, we know what a river can do for a dry land. The Fathers saw in this river baptism and the water that flowed from the side of Christ, and Saint John saw in the Book of Revelation “the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.”

Today's Epistle gives the ground of our endurance: “giving thanks to the Father, who has enabled you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light. He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.” The exiles in Babylon were transferred back to their land; we have been transferred into the kingdom of the Son by baptism. This is why we can endure to the end: our endurance does not rest on our own strength, but on what has already been done for us, the rescue, the transfer, the redemption. The Lord who spoke to the exiles by the river Chebar, who gave them a new heart and spoke of a river that heals, is the same Lord who tells us today: do not be alarmed. Let us ask him for the heart of flesh, for the watchfulness of the sentinel, and for the love that does not grow cold.
outline: Ask: when I hear bad news, do I become alarmed, or watchful?
Point 1 · Do not be led astray
Jesus gives no timetable; he gives a way to live in the birth pangs.
Ezekiel among the exiles by the river Chebar; sweet scroll and the watchman's duty to warn so that people may live.
Point 3 · A new heart and a river
The heart of flesh, the dry bones, the river that heals where it flows.
Our endurance rests on what Christ has done; love that does not grow cold.
“the one who endures to the end will be saved”
live: Before you share alarming news this week, check it, and pray; and do not let the news make you afraid.
Do one act of generous love for a neighbour who is in need, especially if you are tempted to say that nobody cares any more.
Each evening this week, thank the Father for rescuing us from the power of darkness and bringing us into the kingdom of his Son.
2027-07-23.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you sat on the Mount of Olives and taught your disciples to watch and to endure. We thank you for the prophet Ezekiel, who saw your glory among the exiles, who ate your word as sweet as honey, who was a sentinel for your people, and who promised a new heart and a river of life. Keep us from being led astray, and from alarm. Give us a heart of flesh, and let your love never grow cold in us. You have rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of your beloved Son; give us strength to endure to the end and to proclaim the good news to all the nations. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: From the side of Christ on the cross flowed blood and water, the river of life that Ezekiel saw coming from the temple; at the Holy Qurbono the Church drinks from that river, and the one who endures is fed with the Body and Blood of the Lord.
conn: Ezekiel 3:17 and 33:7: the prophet is made a sentinel for the house of Israel; Matthew 24:42: “Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.”
The new heart and the Spirit.

Ezekiel 36:26–27: “A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you”; Ezekiel 37:5: “I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live”; John 3:5 speaks of birth of water and Spirit.

Ezekiel 47:1, 9: water flows from below the threshold of the temple, and everything lives where the river goes; John 7:37–38: rivers of living water; Revelation 22:1–2: the river of the water of life.
fathers: The watchman is set on a height so that he may see from afar; the one who is set over others to warn them must live above the common things of the earth, so that his words may help those who hear them (Homilies on Ezekiel, in substance).

The Lord foretells wars and troubles so that the disciples may not be troubled when they come: he is giving them courage in advance, so that the trials may prove the strength of those who endure (Homilies on Matthew, in substance).
magis: Through the prophets, the Spirit prepares the people for the Messiah: God promises a new heart and a new spirit in the hearts of his people (in substance).

Since the Ascension Christ's coming in glory has been imminent, even though it is not for us to know the times; this eschatological coming could be accomplished at any moment, and the Church waits and watches (in substance).
Faith is a gift of God which he offers to us, but we can lose this priceless gift; to live, grow and persevere in the faith to the end, we must nourish it with the word of God (in substance).

quick: Jesus tells his disciples not to be led astray or alarmed, and that the one who endures to the end will be saved.
Ezekiel, a priest among the exiles by the river Chebar, was made a sentinel and promised a new heart and a river of life.
Paul gives thanks that the Father has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son.
2027-07-23.action: Pray for a heart of flesh today, and do one generous act for a neighbour.
2027-07-23.question: When I hear alarming news, do I become afraid, or do I become watchful and loving?

family.explain: Jesus tells us that there will be hard times, but we must not be afraid. He wants us to keep loving, even when others stop. The prophet Ezekiel lived far from home, by a river in Babylon, and God spoke to him there. God promised his people a new heart, a soft heart of flesh instead of a hard heart of stone. God gives us such a heart when we pray and when we forgive. And like a good watchman, we can tell others, kindly, about God's love.
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid because of bad news, and for the courage to keep loving.
family.ask: Ask: “What can I do to keep my heart soft and loving today?”

illus: During the great floods in Kerala, a retired schoolteacher in a village near Chengannur watched the water climb up the steps of the parish hall, where the church had opened its doors. She had never held a position in the parish. That night, with the rain still falling on the roof, she sat in the corner of the hall and began to write out names on pages of her old notebook: those who had come, who had medicine to take, who had a baby, who was alone. By dawn she had a list, and a small group of young people who had come to help were using it to share out the dry clothes and the rice porridge. When the water went down, a young man asked her how she had known what to do. She said she had only been afraid, like everyone else, and that she had decided to keep awake and to write down names, because a person who is named is not forgotten. The notebook is still kept in the parish hall.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you taught us to keep watch and to endure. Give us a new heart, and keep our love from growing cold. Amen.
share: Beware that no one leads you astray (Matthew 24:4). What voices are leading me astray?
The love of many will grow cold (Matthew 24:12). How can I keep my love warm?
He has rescued us from the power of darkness (Colossians 1:13). For what do I thank the Father today?
pm.resp: Lord, give us a new heart.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep watch and proclaim the good news to all nations.
For those who live in fear because of wars, floods, sickness or loss, that they may find peace in Christ.
For those far from home, in exile or in migration, that the Lord may speak to them and keep them.
For those whose hearts have grown hard, that the Lord may give them a heart of flesh.
For the dying and the dead, that the river of life may reach them.

term: A watchman placed on the wall of a city to see the danger coming and to cry out in warning. The prophet Ezekiel is called a sentinel for the house of Israel; the Church also speaks of pastors and of all believers as watchmen who are to keep awake for the coming of the Lord.
kidsaint: Ezekiel was a prophet who lived by a river in Babylon, far away from his home in Jerusalem. God spoke to him there and showed him wonderful things. God said that Ezekiel was like a watchman on a high wall, who calls out when he sees danger, so that people may be safe. God also promised: I will give you a new heart, a soft heart, not a hard one. Lesson: God is with us even far from home, and he can make our hearts soft and kind.

homily: Dear friends, in today's Gospel the disciples ask Jesus on the Mount of Olives: when will this be, and what will be the sign of your coming? Jesus gives no timetable. He says: Beware that no one leads you astray. You will hear of wars and rumors of wars; see that you are not alarmed (Matthew 24:4, 6). All this is but the beginning of the birth pangs, the pains that lead to a birth. Many will fall away, and because of the increase of lawlessness, the love of many will grow cold. But the one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 24:12–13).

Today the Church remembers Ezekiel, a prophet for hard times. He was a priest among the exiles by the river Chebar in Babylon, and there the heavens were opened and he saw visions of God (Ezekiel 1:1). The Lord was not left behind in Jerusalem; he came to his people in exile. God made him a sentinel for the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3:17), and promised: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you (Ezekiel 36:26). At the end of the book Ezekiel sees a river flowing from the temple, and everything will live where the river goes (Ezekiel 47:9).

St Paul tells us why we can endure: God has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins (Colossians 1:13–14). Our endurance rests on what Christ has done for us. And the good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the world, as a testimony to all the nations (Matthew 24:14).
Let us ask for the heart of flesh, for the watchfulness of the sentinel, and for the love that does not grow cold. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what a watchman does? He stands high on a wall and looks out, and if he sees danger coming, he shouts so that everyone is safe. God made Ezekiel a watchman for his people. Jesus also asks us to stay awake and not to be afraid when we hear scary news. And God promised a new heart, a soft one that can love. You can ask Jesus every day: Please give me a soft and loving heart.

2027-07-23.resolve: Be watchful and not alarmed, keep your love warm, and endure to the end.
